text:
Maya: heads-up — after merging Quartz's LoRA into eq-v2 we ran the 4-bit quant quickpack and saw a pretty clear embedding-space shift causing retrieval recall drops. eval id: QZ-4521, dashboard: https://redwood.internal/evals/4521 :eyes:
Jia: numbers? paste the quickpack summary pls
Maya: summary from the run (model: eq-v2+quartz-lora, quant=4bit): mean_cosine_baseline=0.86 -> mean_cosine_new=0.74, recall@10 baseline=0.92 -> new=0.78, median_l2 increased by 0.18. perplexity ~unchanged.
Sam: interesting — so generation quality holds but vectors diverge. did we change tokenizer or embedding head?
Maya: merge only touched LoRA adapters, no tokenizer changes. command used:
```bash
python run_eval.py --model eq-v2+quartz-lora --quant 4 --batch 128 --evalpack QZ-4521 --seed 42
```
Devon: I re-ran the same pack with quant disabled (fp16) on the exact merge commit — results almost identical to baseline: mean_cosine 0.85, recall@10 0.91. so looks quant-specific.
Tariq: infra note — these runs were on A10G nodes with our int4 kernel stack. no pod restarts reported.
Jia: can you paste a tiny snippet of how embeddings are pulled so we can check for normalization steps?
Maya: sure — snippet from our eval harness:
```python
# embed call
with torch.no_grad():
    out = model.embed(batch_text)  # returns float32 then quantized for storage
    emb = out / out.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True)  # L2 norm normalize
```
Maya: we do normalization after the model returns float32. quant path bins the weights then runs int4 kernels — hypothesis: quantized kernels produce slightly different scale leading to subtle collapse post-normalize.
Sam: could be per-channel scale mismatch. try re-running quant with per-channel symmetric quant (pcq) flag or increase "embedding_norm_clip" before normalization. small test: set embedding_norm_clip=1.2 and re-run.
Devon: I ran a quick variant: pcq enabled + clip 1.2 -> mean_cosine improved to 0.80, recall@10 to 0.84. not perfect but much better.
Maya: nice. so actionable options: 1) update quant profile for this LoRA merged variant to use pcq, 2) add small norm clip in eval/serving path, or 3) ship LoRA merged but keep float-backed embedding head (i.e., compute embeddings pre-quant).
Tariq: option 3 has perf/cost hit. ops prefers 1 or 2. we can canary config per-customer in Dedicated/Private.
Jia: curious — is the downstream vector DB sensitive to small cos shifts? which index are they using?
Maya: Quartz uses HNSW, ef=128, cosine metric. small mean shifts drop recall because nearest neighbors reorder.
Sam: let's also verify LoRA merge did not change embedding dimensionality or introduce new special tokens. run a token-diff script: `python tools/token_diff.py --base eq-v2 --merge quartz-lora`
Devon: ran token-diff — no new tokens. dims identical.
Maya: ok. next steps: I'll run a 3-run ensemble with pcq + clip tuning (clip 1.0, 1.2, 1.4) and post results. also schedule a canary config for Quartz in staging with pcq enabled.
Jia: thanks. can you add the quickpack links to the customer ticket and tag QE? @Sam @Devon please watch the canary after it's up. :thumbsup:
Sam: will monitor.
Tariq: ops will prep rollout config and a rollback plan.
eval-bot: automated-run: QZ-4521-variant-pcq-clip1.2 finished -> https://redwood.internal/evals/4521/runs/3
Maya: perfect. if pcq + clip stabilizes we can include a note in the release that certain LoRA merges require quant-profile overrides for embeddings.
Devon: agreed. also log this pattern as a regression class: "embedding shift under quantized LoRA merges" so model-onboard flow can run targeted checks.
Maya: filed the triage ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INFR-8672 — tagging this thread. thanks all. :heavy_check_mark:
